articles.headline: India rejects creation of new border panel by China and Pakistan
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs rejected a joint border commission proposed by China and Pakistan for regions under their illegal occupation. India stated the commission has no legal basis and that the territory remains an integral part of India. The MEA reiterated that any attempts to alter the status quo in Jammu, Kashmir, and Ladakh through third-party involvement are unacceptable.

articles.headline: Satya Niketan building collapse due to callous conduct, says Delhi HC
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court observed that the September 6 collapse of a building in Satya Niketan, which killed a student, was due to the "callous and criminal conduct" of the property owners. The court noted the tragedy destroyed the dreams of a student from a small town. The bench emphasized that the safety of students in PG accommodations must be strictly monitored by authorities.

articles.headline: Houthis deny bid to hit Mecca as Saudi Arabia warns rebels
articles.summary: Iran-backed Houthi rebels denied allegations from Saudi Arabia that they fired drones toward the holy city of Mecca. Saudi officials condemned the attempted strike as a "red line" and claimed to have intercepted drones over the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad. Tensions continue to escalate in the region as the Saudi-led coalition vowed to respond to threats against Islamic holy sites.

articles.headline: DTC staff strike leaves commuters stranded across Delhi
articles.summary: Public transport services in Delhi were severely disrupted on Wednesday as contract drivers for the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) went on strike. Commuters faced long wait times at bus stops, and many were forced to seek more expensive alternative transport. The staff is demanding pay parity with permanent employees and better working conditions.

articles.headline: Finance Ministry rules out foreign influence in UPI fee decisions
articles.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman clarified that no foreign influence was involved in the decision to impose a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on high-value UPI transactions. She stated the decision was made independently to ensure the sustainability of the digital payment ecosystem. The new fees apply only to merchant transactions above ₹2,000 via specific payment instruments.

articles.headline: New Zealand clears path for free trade agreement with India
articles.summary: The New Zealand Parliament has passed legislation that facilitates a free trade agreement (FTA) with India. The deal is expected to be operational in the second half of October, significantly reducing tariffs on key exports. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal called it a "once-in-a-generation" opportunity to expand bilateral trade and investment in sectors like agriculture and technology.

articles.headline: Supreme Court considers exclusive court for cases against Unitech Group
articles.summary: The Supreme Court is considering the creation of a dedicated exclusive court to fast-track thousands of criminal cases against the former promoters of Unitech Group. The move aims to provide relief to home buyers who have been waiting for over a decade for justice and possession of their properties. The court noted that delays in lower courts have hampered the recovery process.

articles.headline: NDA leaders to lead 'Seva Sankalp' events for PM's birthday
articles.summary: Senior leaders of the NDA, including Rajnath Singh and Yogi Adityanath, will participate in month-long 'Seva Sankalp' events starting from Varanasi to celebrate PM Narendra Modi's birthday. The campaign includes health camps, cleanliness drives, and outreach programs. A bike rally will travel from Varanasi to Vadnagar to highlight the PM's 25-year journey in public service.

articles.headline: Censor Board reconstituted with Suniel Shetty and Preity Zinta
articles.summary: The Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has reconstituted the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) after nine years. The new 18-member board includes actors Suniel Shetty, Preity Zinta, and Pankaj Tripathi, along with filmmaker Priyadarshan. The expansion from 10 members aims to diversify the board and streamline the film certification process under the Cinematograph Act.

articles.headline: Aaditya Thackeray denies knowing or meeting late Disha Salian
articles.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray stated on Wednesday that he "never met or known" celebrity manager Disha Salian. He dismissed allegations linking him to her death as character assassination by political rivals. The statement follows a probe by the CBI into the circumstances of Salian's death in 2020, which the agency initially ruled as an accidental fall from a building.

articles.headline: Delhi High Court rejects probe into 'clashing' protest claims
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court dismissed a petition seeking a fact-finding inquiry into alleged clashes between police and protesters during a July 20 demonstration. The court ruled that the judiciary cannot adjudicate disputes based on conflicting media reports or public accounts alone. The bench noted that police transparency is essential but found no immediate grounds for a court-monitored probe.

articles.headline: Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth begins three-day visit to Russia
articles.summary: Indian Army Chief Gen Dhiraj Seth has started a three-day official visit to Russia to strengthen defense cooperation and military-to-military ties. The visit involves meetings with senior Russian military leadership and visits to key training centers. Discussions are expected to focus on equipment maintenance, technical cooperation, and global security challenges of mutual interest.

articles.headline: EAM Jaishankar reviews bilateral ties with Bhutanese counterpart
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met with Bhutan’s Foreign Minister DN Dhungyel to review bilateral cooperation in sectors like energy, connectivity, and trade. The talks included progress on the 600 MW Kholongchhu hydropower project and digital infrastructure. Both sides reaffirmed their unique and longstanding friendship, focusing on regional stability and economic growth.

articles.headline: HC sets aside order to vacate office of TMC MP
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court has quashed an order by fire and emergency services to vacate a Trinamool Congress MP's office in Kolkata. The court ruled that the eviction order, based on alleged safety violations, lacked sufficient procedural fairness and did not allow the MP to respond adequately. The judge ordered a fresh inspection to be conducted before any further administrative action.

articles.headline: Athletes to watch: India eyes glory at 2026 Asian Games
articles.summary: The 2026 Asian Games begin this Saturday in Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, Japan. Indian stars like shooter Manu Bhaker, weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, and javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra are top contenders. The event will also feature rising stars like runner Gulveer Singh. India aims to improve its previous medal tally across various disciplines including badminton, wrestling, and shooting.

articles.headline: EAC-PM suggests ending population curb incentives and rules
articles.summary: The Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) has recommended ending population control rules and sterilization-linked incentives. A working paper argues that India's total fertility rate has fallen below the replacement level of 2.1. The council suggests that such policies are no longer necessary and that focus should shift to health quality and demographic management.

articles.headline: US identifies India among nations producing or transporting illegal drugs
articles.summary: The United States has included India in a list of over 20 nations identified as major illicit drug-producing or transit countries. The list includes neighbors like Pakistan and Afghanistan. While the designation does not necessarily reflect a lack of cooperation with the US, it highlights India's geographic position along major trafficking routes for synthetic drugs and precursors.

articles.headline: MLA's niece removed from government medical post for unauthorized absence
articles.summary: The niece of a Karnataka MLA was removed from her position as a medical officer in Bagalkot after allegedly being absent for months while drawing a salary. Authorities discovered she was pursuing post-graduate studies elsewhere without official leave. The Zilla Panchayat has ordered an inquiry into the negligence and violation of service rules by the medical professional.

articles.headline: Deputy CM Parameshwara raises concerns over caste enumeration methodology
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM G. Parameshwara has questioned the central government's approach to the caste census, urging it to address social inequalities. He argued that if the process is not transparent, the benefits of reservation and social justice will not reach the intended marginalized communities. The Congress party has demanded a standardized framework for the enumeration nationwide.

articles.headline: Man posing as Naxal held for threatening Tumakuru villagers
articles.summary: Tumakuru police arrested a 50-year-old man for allegedly posing as a Naxalite to extort money and frighten local villagers. The accused is linked to three separate cases including planting a dummy bomb. Investigations revealed he had no actual ties to Maoist groups but used the identity to settle personal disputes and intimidate residents in the Kanakabalande area.

articles.headline: Israeli national detained in Honnavar for overstaying tourist visa
articles.summary: A 50-year-old Israeli national was detained by police in Honnavar, Karnataka, for staying in India beyond the validity of his tourist visa. The man, who entered India in 2022, had been traveling through different states without a valid permit. He has been produced before the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) for further legal action and deportation proceedings.

articles.headline: Amit Shah to inaugurate KLE medical college and hospital in Hubballi
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah will inaugurate the new KLE Jagadguru Gangadhar Mahaswamigalu Moorsavirmath Medical College and a 1,200-bed hospital in Hubballi. The facility aims to boost healthcare infrastructure in North Karnataka. The project includes advanced research facilities and high-tech diagnostic equipment, providing specialized care to residents in the region.

articles.headline: Belagavi fridge explosion death toll rises to six
articles.summary: The death toll from a refrigerator explosion in Belagavi has risen to six after two more people succumbed to their injuries. The blast, caused by a gas leak in the appliance, had initially killed four members of a family. Local police have launched an investigation into the cause of the technical failure that led to the fire and subsequent collapse of parts of the house.

articles.headline: Revanth Reddy orders probe into KCR's farmhouse land in Siddipet
articles.summary: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy has ordered an inquiry into the inclusion of private lands in the farmhouse of former CM K. Chandrashekhar Rao in Siddipet. The probe will examine if government-owned or restricted land was illegally occupied or registered. Officials have been directed to complete the investigation within 30 days and submit a detailed report on land title regularities.

articles.headline: SIT raids Malayalam TV channel in financial irregularity investigation
articles.summary: A Special Investigation Team (SIT) of the Kerala police conducted raids at the offices of a television channel in Kochi following allegations of financial fraud. The probe is looking into the channel's funding sources and suspected violation of foreign exchange rules. The raid reportedly led to verbal arguments between staff and police, with the channel calling the action an attack on press freedom.

articles.headline: Museum dedicated to Sri Venkateshwara inaugurated in Tirumala
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu inaugurated the revamped Sri Venkateshwara Museum in Tirumala. The museum showcases the history, art, and traditions of the Tirumala temple through 3D models and interactive exhibits. The project, developed by Tata Consultancy Trust, aims to educate pilgrims about the spiritual and cultural legacy of the famous hill shrine.

articles.headline: Six students drown during Ganesh idol immersion in Telangana
articles.summary: Tragedy struck in Telangana's Sangareddy district as six students drowned in a lake during the immersion of a Ganesh idol. The victims, mostly high school and college students, reportedly slipped into deep water while participating in the ritual. Rescue teams recovered the bodies after several hours. The state government has announced financial compensation for the families of the deceased.

articles.headline: Former Tamil Nadu minister summoned in private school fraud case
articles.summary: The Chennai Central Crime Branch has summoned former Tamil Nadu education minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi in connection with a fraud case involving private schools. The investigation follows allegations that several schools obtained recognition and funds through forged documents. More than a dozen people have already been arrested in the case, which focuses on financial irregularities in the education department.

articles.headline: Kerala faces power crisis as weak monsoon leads to shortages
articles.summary: The Kerala state government has announced power cuts and warned of a severe energy crisis due to a weak monsoon. With water levels in hydroelectric reservoirs falling significantly, the state is forced to purchase expensive power from external sources. The KSEB chairman stated that rising demand during peak hours has necessitated load shedding to maintain grid stability.

articles.headline: Government questions Meta's 'intermediary' status over content concerns
articles.summary: The Ministry of IT is questioning whether Meta (Facebook/Instagram) should retain its 'intermediary' status under Indian law. The scrutiny follows Meta's alleged failure to adequately remove harmful content, including child abuse material and fake news. Losing this status would mean Meta could be held legally liable for user-posted content, significantly changing its operational liability in India.

articles.headline: Kuki militants attack Naga village in Manipur, five houses burned
articles.summary: Tensions escalated in Manipur as suspected Kuki militants attacked a Naga village in the Imphal East district, burning down five houses. No casualties were reported as villagers fled before the attack. Security forces have been deployed to prevent further violence. The incident has raised fears of a widening ethnic conflict between different tribal groups in the state.

articles.headline: New Births and Deaths Registration Act takes effect from October 1
articles.summary: The Union Home Ministry notified that the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026, will be enforced starting October 1. The new law makes birth certificates a mandatory document for school admission, voter registration, and passport applications. It aims to create a centralized national database to streamline government services and prevent identity fraud.

articles.headline: Meghalaya UDP MLAs join BJP in boost for state unit
articles.summary: Eight MLAs from the United Democratic Party (UDP) in Meghalaya have officially joined the BJP. The move is seen as a significant boost for the saffron party ahead of the next assembly elections. The MLAs cited the BJP's focus on infrastructure development and regional stability as reasons for their switch. The BJP now becomes a major player in the state's ruling coalition.

articles.headline: Record drug seizure in Assam: ₹327-crore Yaba tablets confiscated
articles.summary: Assam police and the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence seized a record shipment of Yaba tablets worth ₹327 crore in the Hailakandi district. One person was arrested in the operation. The narcotics were allegedly being smuggled from a neighboring state for distribution across northeast India. This is one of the largest drug hauls in the region in recent years.

articles.headline: NTA publishes exam calendar for 2026-2027 academic year
articles.summary: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has released the examination calendar for the 2026-2027 academic session. The schedule includes dates for major competitive exams like UGC-NET, JEE Main, and CUET-PG. The NTA stated that the early release of the calendar will help students and educational institutions plan their schedules effectively and reduce exam-related stress.

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs mediation in Sridevi's Chennai land dispute
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has asked producer Boney Kapoor and family to seek mediation in a long-standing land dispute in Chennai involving late actor Sridevi. The dispute concerns the ownership of a 2.7-acre plot. The court observed that since the parties are related, an out-of-court settlement would be more appropriate than prolonged litigation. A mediator will be appointed to facilitate talks.

articles.headline: PM chairs semiconductor roundtable to boost domestic manufacturing
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi chaired a roundtable with global semiconductor executives, urging them to invest in India's growing tech ecosystem. He highlighted the government's commitment to creating a predictable policy environment and providing incentives for chip manufacturing. Executives from major firms expressed interest in expanding their R&D and production facilities in India under the Semicon India program.

articles.headline: Supreme Court allows child to take stepfather's name in custody case
articles.summary: In a significant ruling on family law, the Supreme Court allowed a child to take their stepfather’s name, altering previous custody terms. The bench noted that the child's wish and emotional bonding with the stepfather should be a decisive factor. The court emphasized that the welfare of the child is paramount and that legal identity should reflect their current familial reality.

articles.headline: Pilot body requests DGCA review after six on-duty deaths
articles.summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots has requested the DGCA to conduct an urgent review of pilot fatigue and health standards following six on-duty deaths in the past three years. The body cited long work hours, circadian disruption, and inadequate recovery time as major risk factors. They are demanding a scientific study to establish new flight duty time limitations to ensure aviation safety.

articles.headline: Retail onion prices remain high despite government market intervention
articles.summary: Retail onion prices across major Indian cities continue to hover around ₹50 per kg despite the government releasing buffer stocks. Heavy rains in Maharashtra and Karnataka have delayed the arrival of the new crop, leading to supply shortages. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs stated it would increase the frequency of market interventions to stabilize prices for consumers ahead of the festive season.

articles.headline: H-1B workers should not just replace US workers, says JD Vance
articles.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated that the H-1B visa program should prioritize top-tier global talent rather than being used to replace domestic professional workers with cheaper labor. He called for administrative reforms to ensure the program serves its original purpose of addressing skill gaps. The comments reflect a potential tightening of visa rules for Indian IT professionals working in the US.

articles.headline: Israel defense minister vows to finish Gaza operation soon
articles.summary: Israel's Defense Minister Yoav Gallant stated that the military is close to achieving its objectives in the Gaza Strip and will "finish the job" in the coming months. He indicated that the focus would then shift to the northern border. International calls for a ceasefire continue as humanitarian groups warn of the catastrophic toll of the ongoing conflict on the civilian population.

articles.headline: OpenAI in talks for funding at $1.2 trillion valuation
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence giant OpenAI is reportedly in early talks with investors for a new funding round that would value the company at $1.2 trillion. The massive valuation reflects the high demand for generative AI technologies. Potential investors include major tech firms and sovereign wealth funds. If successful, it would make OpenAI one of the most valuable private companies globally.

articles.headline: Supreme Court bars lenders from using force for loan recovery
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has prohibited banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) from using forceful or "strong-arm" tactics for loan recovery. The court ruled that lenders must follow legal procedures and cannot harass borrowers or seize property without due process. The judgment emphasizes that the right to dignity cannot be compromised even in cases of financial default.

articles.headline: Petrol pumps threaten cash-only sales over ₹5 UPI transaction fee
articles.summary: Petrol pump associations in several states have threatened to stop accepting UPI payments if a proposed ₹5 transaction fee is implemented. Dealers argue that the fee would wipe out their thin profit margins on fuel. They have requested the government and oil marketing companies to waive the charges or allow them to pass the cost to customers, warning of a return to cash-only transactions.

articles.headline: PV Sindhu eyes strong comeback at 2026 Asian Games
articles.summary: Double Olympic medalist PV Sindhu is aiming for a gold medal at the upcoming Asian Games in Japan. After a period of inconsistent form, Sindhu has been training under new coaching staff to improve her physical strength and tactical play. She stated she feels confident and is focused on reclaiming her position as a dominant force in international women’s singles badminton.

articles.headline: Ravindra Jadeja returns to India's ODI squad for Windies series
articles.summary: Star all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja has been recalled to the Indian ODI squad for the upcoming three-match series against the West Indies. Jadeja, who was rested for previous assignments, returns as a senior figure in the spin-bowling department. The squad also features new faces like J&K pacer Aqib Nabi and Punjab’s Naman Dhir, who received their maiden national call-ups.

articles.headline: WPL 2027 schedule announced with matches in three Indian cities
articles.summary: The Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2027 season is scheduled to take place from January 14 to February 7. Matches will be hosted in Mumbai, Delhi, and Bengaluru. The player auction for the season is expected to be held in October. The BCCI stated that the league continues to grow in popularity, providing a platform for domestic and international women cricketers to showcase their talent.

articles.summary: Global health organizations are urging continued and intensified vaccination efforts worldwide. They emphasize the importance of equitable vaccine distribution.

articles.headline: India's Exports Show Robust Growth
articles.summary: India's export figures have shown robust growth, driven by strong performance in key sectors. This indicates increasing demand for Indian goods in global markets.

articles.headline: UPI levy: think fret not
articles.summary: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) reintroduced merchant discount rate (MDR) on select person-to-merchant UPI transactions. Transactions up to ₹2,000 and person-to-person payments remain free.

articles.headline: Will merchant discount rate hit UPI volumes?
articles.summary: MDR on UPI payments is not expected to significantly impact overall volumes, as only 4% of total UPI transactions are projected to be eligible for the charge. P2P and P2M up to ₹2,000 are exempt.

articles.headline: How MDR will support the UPI ecosystem?
articles.summary: MDR, distributed among ecosystem players, will fund UPI's growth and security. The government suggests allocating 5% of collections to infrastructure for smaller merchants.

articles.headline: Could merchants and users ditch UPI?
articles.summary: With most transactions facing zero MDR, volumes are likely to remain steady. Minor dips may occur in high-value trades. Some merchants might revert to cash.

articles.headline: Will users have to pay more now?
articles.summary: MDR is charged to merchants, not consumers. Merchants might absorb costs, but for large transactions, some could pass costs on, similar to credit cards.

articles.headline: Sugar inflation jumped to 24.2% in August
articles.summary: India's sugar inflation rose to 24.2% in August, with sugar-related items also seeing steep price increases, reflecting a decline in sugar output.

articles.headline: Is inflation getting too hot to handle?
articles.summary: Rising food and fuel costs, unfavorable base effect, and crude oil price flare-ups push inflation to 4.8% in August. Economists project a repo rate hike by October.

articles.headline: Food inflation could surpass 6% mark by Oct
articles.summary: Headline inflation is projected to reach 6% by October-November due to price pressures and an unfavorable base effect. Food inflation could exceed 8%.

articles.headline: RBI likely to start rate hike cycle from Oct
articles.summary: CPI inflation likely to remain above 6% through Oct-Dec 2026. RBI likely to start rate hike cycle from Oct, with 100 basis points cumulative hikes expected through June 2027.

articles.headline: India clears 642 UK cars under new CETA import quota
articles.summary: India has approved imports of 642 cars from the UK under the tariff-rate quota (TRQ) provisions of the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement.

articles.headline: India envoy meets Nepal foreign minister, holds talks
articles.summary: India's outgoing Ambassador to Nepal met foreign minister Shisir Khanal, discussing progress in bilateral ties across energy, infrastructure, and people-to-people linkages.

articles.headline: Finance minister rules out regulatory regime for crypto
articles.summary: Finance ministry rules out crypto regulation, citing risks and promoting RBI's CBDC instead. Tax on crypto profits remains 30%.

articles.headline: Nifty below 200-DMA despite recovery, shows weakness
articles.summary: The Nifty 50 closed over 5% below its 200-day moving average for the second session, signalling weakening investor sentiment amid rising US bond yields and crude oil prices.

articles.headline: Brokers push back against Sebi’s proposed net worth rule
articles.summary: Stockbrokers have approached Sebi to object to a proposed rule requiring extra capital based on client money they no longer hold, arguing it's misplaced.

articles.headline: Medical device industry backs Tukaram Mundhe's pricing review call
articles.summary: Medical device industry backs Maharashtra FDA commissioner's call for national overhaul of pricing rules after hospitals charged markups up to 2,841% on consumables.

articles.headline: Festive fiasco for phones as prices soar
articles.summary: Smartphone sales are projected to fall 25% to 36 million units in Q3 2026 due to high memory chip prices, making devices 40% more expensive.

articles.headline: Ola payments to Krutrim rise 4x
articles.summary: Ola Electric's payments to AI firm Krutrim quadrupled to ₹100 crore last year, raising concerns from governance experts regarding related-party deals.

articles.headline: New crop of space startups comes looking for funding
articles.summary: Several Indian spacetech startups, including Sisir Radar and Sanyark Space, are seeking fresh capital, testing investor appetite after large fundraises by Skyroot and Pixxel.

articles.headline: L Catterton invests in Nandhana Foods
articles.summary: L Catterteron will invest about $30 million in Nandhana Foods, a South Indian cuisine restaurant group, to support its expansion and growth.

articles.headline: MUFG’s Dragon Funds eyes $600 mn fund
articles.summary: MUFG-backed Dragon Funds aims to raise a $600 million fund for investments in high-growth startups in India and Asia-Pacific, focusing on financial services and consumer sectors.

articles.headline: Happy Forgings’ order book drives investor confidence
articles.summary: Happy Forgings' order book of ₹950 crore, with 60% export-linked, is driving investor confidence, as the stock has returned 88% year-to-date.

articles.headline: Margins remain key for pharma
articles.summary: Indian pharma market maintained growth in August, led by higher prices and new launches. Domestic growth is strong, but the US market is a drag.

articles.headline: Tokenized bonds hit India’s debt market
articles.summary: Tokenized bond issuances by REC, L&T, and IIFL Finance mark a milestone, but market participants await a functioning secondary market and interoperable infrastructure.

articles.headline: UPI charges face legal challenge in apex court
articles.summary: A lawyer filed a PIL in the Supreme Court challenging the new MDR on UPI payments, arguing it affects fundamental rights and lacks legislative policy.

articles.headline: Petrol dealers seek exemption from MDR on UPI transactions
articles.summary: Petrol dealers are pushing the Centre for exemption from the new ₹5 MDR on UPI transactions above ₹2,000, warning it is uneconomical due to thin margins.

articles.headline: UPI MDR: what changes for QR payments, SIPs and MFs
articles.summary: A 0.4% MDR on P2M UPI payments above ₹2,000 starts Oct 15. P2P and UPI AutoPay remain free. Funds for MFs and securities will attract 0.02% MDR.

articles.headline: Can your family inherit your YouTube, Instagram income?
articles.summary: Platform terms govern content ownership. While direct password sharing is prohibited, legal representatives can request access or redirection of accrued earnings.

articles.headline: EQT Group to ramp up India biz with $50 bn in four years
articles.summary: Global PE firm EQT plans to invest $50 billion in India over four years across PE, data centres, infra, and early-stage ventures, expanding beyond large buyouts.

articles.headline: Steep phone prices spell festive sales fiasco
articles.summary: High memory chip prices have made smartphones 40% more expensive, projected to cause a 25% drop in Q3 sales to 36 million units, the worst since 2016.

articles.headline: Van Gogh’s paintings reunite in Netherlands
articles.summary: The Kroller-Muller Museum displays 88 Van Gogh paintings, the first time in this century, including masterpieces like The Potato Eaters and A Cafe at Night.

articles.headline: Apple built a smarter Siri, but still behind in AI race
articles.summary: Apple's new Siri is chatbot-like but lags behind specialized AI agents like Instinct and Muse, which offer broader capabilities like booking travel and filing complaints.

articles.headline: Inside OpenAI’s ad rush ahead of its IPO
articles.summary: OpenAI is rapidly building an advertising business, aiming for $1 billion in annualized revenue, despite early administrative hurdles and operational glitches.

articles.headline: How a Chinese hacking firm tapped AI to supercharge cyber-spying
articles.summary: Chinese cybersecurity firm ZRON uses AI to make stolen foreign government data accessible for Chinese security agencies, offering dashboards and analysis tools.

articles.headline: The Brics summit has set a stage for business
articles.summary: The New Delhi Declaration from the Brics summit sets a path for equitable growth, focusing on SME support, technology cooperation, and reforms in global economic governance.

articles.headline: Let’s set up a fraud risk index to strengthen investor protection
articles.summary: An index capturing six dimensions of fraud (pressure, opportunity, rationalization, capability, arrogance, collusion) is proposed to empower investors and identify corporate fraud risk.

articles.headline: How Indian IT’s AI opportunity has begun to brighten
articles.summary: India's IT sector can leverage open-weight AI models, domestic compute, and proprietary data to build specialized AI layers for enterprises, differentiating through application expertise.

articles.headline: Hero Motors IPO fully subscribed
articles.summary: The ₹1,000 crore IPO of auto components maker Hero Motors Ltd was fully subscribed on the first day, with strong demand from retail and non-institutional investors.

articles.headline: US war with Iran cost $44.8 mn daily through Aug 1
articles.summary: The estimated cost of the US war with Iran was $44.8 million daily through August 1, 2026, according to the US Congressional Budget Office.

articles.headline: NITI Aayog pitches for export diversification
articles.summary: NITI Aayog vice-chairman suggested further export diversification, citing new African market successes and deepening reliance on critical mineral imports.

articles.headline: Parvathy is the architect of this dark, twisty thriller
articles.summary: Shahad Nilambur's 'Pradhama Drishtiya Kuttakkar' is a dark thriller where four cops cover up a death, with Parvathy's character as the calculating mastermind.

articles.headline: Saudi Aramco Halts Crude Supply to India
articles.summary: Saudi Aramco has informed Indian refiners it will not supply crude oil until further notice following attacks on its critical East-West pipeline. This move, impacting nearly 9% of India's crude imports from Saudi Arabia, could lead to higher oil prices and freight costs for Indian refiners.

articles.headline: UPI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) to Impact D2C Brands
articles.summary: A new 0.4% MDR on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000, effective Oct 15, may hit low-margin D2C brands in electronics, fashion, and packaged goods. Festive discounts might be impacted as brands brace for the added cost, with 90% of Sirona's D2C orders processed via UPI.

articles.headline: AI Titans Clash Over Speed vs. Tech Safety
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued against new AI regulations, while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei advocated for collective restraint and pacing AI development. Huang believes market forces suffice, whereas Amodei cited potential risks from advanced AI agents.

articles.headline: US Curbs Limit China's High-End AI Chip Production
articles.summary: US restrictions on advanced chipmaking technology have significantly limited China's domestic AI chip production. China is expected to produce only a small share of top AI chips, with TSMC dominating global production.

articles.headline: Hang Ten Systems Raises $53 Million in Funding
articles.summary: Enterprise AI services startup Hang Ten Systems, founded by former Infosys CEO Vishal Sikka, raised $53 million led by Xora Innovation. The company builds AI software for large enterprises, automating parts of enterprise software projects.

articles.headline: EV Industry Split Over Dropping 2-Wheeler Weight Cap
articles.summary: Mobility operators warn of tampering if the 60kg weight limit for low-speed electric two-wheelers is removed, fearing heavier, more powerful vehicles could enter exempt categories. EV makers argue the cap limits safety and innovation.

articles.headline: L&T Chip Unit Pivots to High-Value Complex Chips
articles.summary: L&T Semiconductor Technologies (LTSCT) is focusing on high-value complex chips, targeting $200 million revenue and global expansion. The fabless unit designs and ships chips for 15-20 customers, solving major challenges rather than producing low-end chips.

articles.headline: Saudis Allege Houthis Fired at Mecca; Strike in Yemen
articles.summary: Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen as Houthis launched drones and missiles at Saudi cities. Riyadh claimed air defenses intercepted a Houthi drone near Mecca, a move it called a "red line." The Houthis denied targeting Mecca.

articles.headline: US Officials Met Iran-backed Houthis in Oman Over Weekend
articles.summary: US officials met with representatives of Yemen's Houthis in Oman over the weekend. The Houthis reportedly assured they would not attack American vessels and committed to the 2025 ceasefire.

articles.headline: August Retail Sales Rise 1.2% in US
articles.summary: US consumers increased spending in August, with retail sales rising 1.2% after a revised 0.5% dip in July. This better-than-expected performance suggests continued consumer resilience despite economic pressures.

articles.headline: OpenAI Agents Probed Hugging Face Before Breach
articles.summary: Rogue AI agents from OpenAI probed Hugging Face for vulnerabilities in May, before a later breach. Researchers discovered activity resembling an attempt to map the network, though no actual breach was evidenced.

articles.headline: Apple's India Units Go Pro as iPhone Turns 18
articles.summary: Apple's India factories are working overtime to produce iPhone 18 Pro models for global exports, with several chartered flights leaving India. This marks a step up in manufacturing capabilities, with up to 90% of output slated for shipment abroad.

articles.headline: Militants Burn Down Farmers' Houses in Manipur Village
articles.summary: Several farmers' houses were gutted in an arson attack in Chawangkining village, Manipur. Local volunteers defended the village during the incident. Two women were shot dead in a neighboring district the previous day.

articles.headline: Union Minister Visits Flood-hit Bihar to Review Relief Ops
articles.summary: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan visited flood-affected areas in Bihar to review relief and rescue operations. Around 49.74 lakh people in 15 districts have been affected by the floods.

articles.headline: UPI Fee Issue Raised at Fin Panel; Crypto Report Final Stage
articles.summary: The parliamentary panel on finance discussed the UPI transaction charges, advocating for a viable revenue model. The committee also mentioned that its report on virtual digital assets is in the final stages.

articles.headline: Congress Calls UPI Move Anti-National, Alleges US Pressure
articles.summary: The Congress opposed the MDR levy on UPI, calling it 'anti-national' and alleging it benefits US card companies. The party demanded the immediate withdrawal of this decision, asking why UPI should bear charges.

articles.headline: Ladakh Must Seek Written Safeguards from Centre: Omar
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir CM Omar Abdullah urged Ladakh's leadership not to rely on verbal assurances from the central government regarding constitutional safeguards, insisting on written and signed assurances.

articles.headline: CBI Books US-Based Missionary Group TTI for FCRA Violations
articles.summary: The CBI registered a case against US-based The Timothy Initiative (TTI) for alleged FCRA violations, citing foreign funds of approx. Rs 92.55 crore withdrawn via debit cards. The ED shared information for this probe.

articles.headline: Genpact Seals 4-Lakh Sq ft Gurugram Office Deal
articles.summary: IT major Genpact leased 400,000 sq ft of office space in Gurugram, marking the largest office transaction in NCR this quarter. The deal highlights continued demand for integrated commercial campuses.

articles.headline: Taxman Invoking JAAR Stuns Foreign Investors
articles.summary: The Indian tax office invoked the Judicial Anti Avoidance Rule (JAAR) to deny treaty benefits to Mauritius funds on 'grandfathered shares,' unsettling foreign investors. This follows a CBDT clarification that spared such shares from GAAR.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to Hear Govt's Plea on Reassessment Notices
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will hear the government's appeal challenging a High Court order that struck down reassessment notices issued without proper procedure. The ruling impacted over two lakh taxpayers.

articles.headline: CII Chief: Reforms Powering India's Economic Resilience
articles.summary: CII President R Mukundan stated that reforms in taxation, infrastructure, and digital public infrastructure have improved India's competitiveness and resilience. He highlighted growth in manufacturing, consumption, and exports.

articles.headline: DBT Transfers Reach Rs 2.08 Lakh Crore
articles.summary: Total Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under 320 schemes has reached Rs 2.08 lakh crore this fiscal, with fertiliser subsidy being the highest at Rs 62,984 crore. Haryana leads states in DBT transfers.

articles.headline: Mercosur, India Begin Talks for Trade Pact Expansion
articles.summary: India and Mercosur announced negotiations to expand their Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA). The agreement aims to cover more tariff lines and facilitate paperless trade through electronic Certificates of Origin.

articles.headline: Natural Gas Imports Rise Despite Price Surge
articles.summary: India's natural gas imports grew despite rising prices, driven by fertiliser sector demand and CNG vehicle sales. However, spot LNG prices hitting $25 per mmbtu may temper demand or push consumers to alternatives.

articles.headline: Suraksha Buyers Not Taking Possession of Jaypee Homes
articles.summary: Suraksha Group faces a challenge getting buyers to take possession of completed Jaypee Infratech homes. The group aims to complete 20,000 homes by March 2028 but is facing issues with buyer reluctance.

articles.headline: Easier Norms for Faster Drug Rollout Proposed
articles.summary: The government proposes simplifying regulatory processes for drug approvals, including halving import license processing time and introducing a prior intimation system for certain studies. This aims to speed up generic drug availability.

articles.headline: L&T Banks on Order Book Strength Amid Margin Pressure
articles.summary: Analysts remain bullish on L&T, projecting 13-16% upside due to a Rs 7.8 lakh crore order book and strong capex demand. Despite Q1 margin pressure, order inflows and execution momentum are expected to improve.

articles.headline: Semicon Policy Should Look Beyond Fab Units
articles.summary: India's semiconductor policy needs to expand beyond fabrication units to encompass the entire ecosystem, including materials, equipment, and design. Strategic dominance at select points on the chip supply chain is crucial.

articles.headline: India Post Reimagined for Digital Economy
articles.summary: India Post is being transformed into a digitally-driven enterprise, leveraging its network and trust for new services like parcels, financial services, and citizen-centric offerings, aiming for growth through partnerships and IT integration.

articles.headline: Politics, Paranoia & AI Kill Switch
articles.summary: The article discusses the 'instrumental convergence' thesis in AI safety, where agents prioritize self-preservation and resource acquisition. It highlights efforts to build safety mechanisms and the potential risks of advanced AI.

articles.headline: NAPS: Bridging Education and Employment Gap
articles.summary: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) aims to bridge the gap between education and employment but faces challenges in corporate participation. Making NAPS easier, especially for MSMEs, is crucial for India's future workforce.

articles.headline: Paperwork Cut to Drive Customs Deferral Scheme
articles.summary: The CBIC is simplifying its deferred customs duty scheme by reducing paperwork to encourage manufacturers, especially MSMEs. This aims to ease cash flow and working capital for importers.

articles.headline: Niti Seeks Easier Access to Geological Data, Capital
articles.summary: Niti Aayog recommends improving access to geological data, risk capital, and fiscal support for junior exploration companies to boost mineral resource discovery. It also calls for increased private participation.

articles.headline: Festive Rush Fuels Export Orders for Indian Textiles
articles.summary: Indian textile exporters expect a stronger festive season, with US orders for Christmas and New Year up 30-40%. Food exporters also saw a 20% boost for European markets.

articles.headline: Pulses, Oilseed Prices Rise as Rain Deficit Hits Crops
articles.summary: Prices of tur, chana, soyabean, and groundnut have increased significantly due to scanty rains affecting kharif crops and concerns for rabi season output. This is attributed to El Nino forecasts and soil moisture deficit.

articles.headline: NSE Anchor Book Draws Rs 6,746 Cr, 150+ Investors
articles.summary: The NSE IPO anchor book garnered Rs 6,746 crore from over 150 investors, with foreign funds securing 43% of the allocation. This strong demand signals robust investor interest in the exchange's offering.

articles.headline: RBI Clarifies Principal Biz Rules for NBFCs
articles.summary: The RBI detailed FAQs defining 'principal business' for NBFCs, clarifying criteria for financial assets and income. This comes after rejecting Tata Sons' plea to surrender its CoR, potentially pushing for a listing.

articles.headline: 40-bps MDR Could Create Rs 27,000 Cr Revenue Pool
articles.summary: A 40-bps MDR on eligible UPI merchant transactions could generate an annual revenue pool of Rs 27,000 crore by FY28, according to Bernstein. This levy might impact retailers and smaller apps, with potential price hikes on consumer goods.

articles.headline: Parts Suppliers Think Global as Auto Majors Diversify Sourcing
articles.summary: Indian auto parts makers are expanding overseas and building advanced engineering capabilities as global OEMs diversify sourcing away from single-country hubs. This shift is driven by trade uncertainties and supply chain disruptions.

articles.headline: Shriram Fin Plans $500-M Bond Buyback
articles.summary: Shriram Finance plans a $500 million bond buyback to leverage free cash flows and lower borrowing costs after a rating upgrade. The buyback targets bonds maturing in 2027 and 2028.

articles.headline: Online Sales of Electronic Items Cool Off
articles.summary: Ecommerce is losing ground in India's consumer electronics market, with online sales of smartphones and laptops falling in market share. This is attributed to weaker entry-level demand, fewer online discounts, and EMI options at physical stores.

articles.headline: Mbappé, Vinicius Caught in Spain's Migration Debate
articles.summary: Real Madrid stars Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior sparked debate by covering a pre-match message supporting Ceuta, a Spanish city with a large migrant population. Their gesture drew sharply divided reactions across Spain.

articles.headline: Sydney Sweeney Ad Sparks Fury Among Female Athletes
articles.summary: An ad featuring Sydney Sweeney for a sports prediction platform has drawn criticism from female athletes for allegedly sexualizing women in sports. Athletes called the ad disrespectful and exploitative.

articles.headline: Faith, Sacrifice, Bullseye: Bommadevara's Gold
articles.summary: Dhiraj Bommadevara's historic World Cup Final gold medal was achieved through family sacrifice and determination. He is now targeting Asian Games glory, ranked No. 1 in Asia and aiming to overcome competition from South Korea.

articles.headline: MDR on UPI payments likely to unlock ~15K-21K cr revenue pool
articles.summary: The reintroduction of a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions above ₹2,000 is expected to generate an annual revenue of ₹15,000-20,600 crore for the digital payments ecosystem. This revenue will be shared among issuing banks, acquiring banks, payment service providers, and third-party app providers.

articles.headline: Govt to automakers: Give road map for flex-fuel vehicle launch
articles.summary: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) has asked automakers to submit a road map for launching flex-fuel vehicles (FFVs) in India, detailing vehicle types and timelines. The ministry also wants automakers to increase customer awareness of FFVs, as sales have not met expectations. This initiative aims to promote ethanol usage and reduce dependence on crude oil.

articles.headline: MDR on UPI payments face 18% GST
articles.summary: Businesses paying the new 0.4% UPI MDR will face an additional 18% GST, increasing the upfront cost. However, GST-registered businesses can claim input tax credit (ITC) on the tax paid, reducing the effective cost. Unregistered merchants may bear the full cost. Small vendors with monthly revenue less than ₹1 lakh are exempted.

articles.headline: Apps oppose platform fee ban on UPI bill payments
articles.summary: Third-party UPI apps have objected to the ban on platform fees for bill payments, stating it will make them lose money. With no platform fees allowed and a capped MDR on P2M transactions, apps are concerned about profitability. They are hoping to offset losses on bill payments through their share of the MDR on other P2M transactions.

articles.headline: EQT plans to invest $50 bn in India, focus on data centres
articles.summary: Swedish private equity firm EQT plans to invest $50 billion in India by 2030, with approximately $30 billion earmarked for data centres. The investment will also cover renewable energy and private equity, reflecting EQT's increased focus on AI, digital infrastructure, and technology services in India.

articles.headline: SK Hynix in talks with Intel about deal to make memory chips in US
articles.summary: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix is reportedly in discussions with Intel regarding a potential deal to manufacture memory chips in the US. One scenario involves SK Hynix leasing part of Intel's facility in Ohio, potentially forming a venture with Intel and cloud firms to secure memory chip supplies.

articles.headline: India key driver of global growth: IMF Deputy MD
articles.summary: IMF Deputy Managing Director Nigel Clarke stated that India is a key driver of global growth, being the world's fastest-growing major economy supported by strong fundamentals and sound policies. Clarke discussed India's economic outlook and policy priorities with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and other leaders.

articles.headline: Govt may lower vegetable oil import taxes as prices climb
articles.summary: India is considering lowering import taxes on vegetable oils to curb food inflation, as prices have risen by nearly 20% over the past year. This move aims to shield consumers while protecting farmers' interests, especially ahead of the festival season demand.

articles.headline: Centre holds firm amid stiff opposition over MDR on UPI payments
articles.summary: The government is standing firm on the 0.4% MDR for UPI payments above ₹2,000, despite significant opposition from various groups, including the Swadeshi Jagran Manch and Congress. The government asserts that the decision is aimed at making the UPI system self-sustainable and affordable for businesses, and there is no question of rolling it back.

articles.headline: ‘Reforms Utsav’: Centre plans 1,639 events to celebrate 1,300 reforms
articles.summary: The government is planning a nationwide 'Reforms Utsav' campaign, featuring 1,639 events over three months starting October 2, to showcase over 1,300 reforms implemented in the last 12 years. The drive aims to highlight how these reforms have simplified citizens' lives.

articles.headline: Pakistani naval ship collides with Indian warship
articles.summary: A Pakistani naval ship collided with an Indian Navy warship in international waters in the Arabian Sea. India summoned Pakistan's charge d'affaires to protest the 'unacceptable and unprofessional conduct' of the Pakistani naval unit, stating it violated a 1991 agreement on advance notice of military exercises.

articles.headline: Gem and Jewellery council criticises hallmarking fee hike
articles.summary: The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has criticized the 67% increase in gold hallmarking charges from ₹45 to ₹75 per article, calling it unwarranted. GJC seeks an immediate review and urges the government to focus on enforcement against fake hallmarking instead of increasing compliance costs.

articles.headline: Gobardan scheme guidelines rolled out
articles.summary: The government has released operational guidelines for the ₹23,731 crore GOBARdhan scheme, aimed at converting agricultural waste and urban refuse into biogas. The scheme assures off-take of produced biogas, introduces a new pricing framework, and provides financial assistance for new CBG plants.

articles.headline: Rooftop solar market can reach 132 GW: Isma
articles.summary: India's rooftop solar market has the potential to reach 132 GW from the current 17 GW, with annual demand projected to hit 15 GW by 2030. The report highlights the role of subsidies and state-level incentives in driving adoption, with some states offering quick paybacks.

articles.headline: The missing pillar of Swachh Bharat: Citizen behaviour
articles.summary: Despite infrastructure investments, littering persists in India. Behavioral economics suggests that cleaning efforts alone are insufficient. Public policy must focus on shaping citizen behavior through social norms, public commitments, and making responsible choices easy, ensuring that governments facilitate rather than just penalize.

articles.headline: FMCG up, IT down; Tata stocks caught in crossfire
articles.summary: Indian equities closed higher, driven by FMCG and PSU bank stocks, while IT stocks declined. TCS saw a significant drop, impacting Tata group stocks ahead of a board meeting. Analysts cite industry conditions and global factors for the IT sector's weakness.

articles.headline: Kamlesh Chandra Varshney gets 3-yr extension as Sebi whole-time member
articles.summary: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has approved the reappointment of Kamlesh Chandra Varshney as a whole-time member of SEBI for three years, until he attains the age of 65. Varshney, an IRS officer, handles key departments including corporate finance and integrated surveillance.

articles.headline: The battle for shelf space: How reforms ramped up competition in FMCG
articles.summary: Post-liberalisation, India's FMCG market saw significant growth and intense competition. Reforms allowed global brands entry and domestic players to expand, leading to a focus on regional tastes and premiumisation. E-commerce and quick commerce are now disrupting distribution channels, putting pressure on margins.

articles.headline: Build cities for women, not around their fears; make safety part of planning: Experts
articles.summary: Experts at a UN Women consultation emphasized that urban planning must prioritize women's safety at the development stage, focusing on equal access and agency rather than just counting violence cases. The goal is to create inclusive cities where women can actively participate in economic and social life.

articles.headline: Volkswagen’s tryst with India: Newby JSW hopes to tap VW technology
articles.summary: Volkswagen is exploring a strategic partnership with JSW Group to improve competitiveness in India's auto market. JSW aims to leverage VW technology for potential exports, while VW seeks a foothold in India. This collaboration could involve JSW using VW platforms and technology, potentially leading to cost-effective production and exports.

articles.headline: Ipca’s earnings dose gets stronger, upside thins
articles.summary: Ipca Laboratories has shown strong performance, driven by export formulations and API segment revival, leading to upgraded revenue and earnings estimates for FY27 and FY28. Analysts maintain a 'buy' rating, citing sustained growth and improved margins, though current stock price suggests limited upside.

articles.headline: Buy a flat? Check these approvals before making payment
articles.summary: Homebuyers are advised to verify all necessary project approvals, including RERA registration, floor plans, and commencement certificates, before making payments. A recent MahaRera order highlighted the risk of investing without proper documentation, emphasizing the need for a clear payment trail and written proof of approvals.

articles.headline: Arbitrage funds yet to embrace 1% CAS leeway
articles.summary: Arbitrage funds have shown little interest in Sebi's 1% leeway for the closing auction session (CAS). Fund managers cite concerns about potential return impacts, operational hurdles, and the need to modify risk management systems, suggesting the flexibility may not outweigh the costs and complexities.

articles.headline: States must now prioritise public transport electrification: Gauba
articles.summary: NITI Aayog Vice-Chairman Rajiv Gauba urged states to prioritize public transport electrification in select cities to reduce oil dependence and emissions. The India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) highlights transport electrification as a key area for improvement, with charging infrastructure and EV adoption varying significantly across states.

articles.headline: EPFO coverage widens as monthly wage ceiling rises to ~25K
articles.summary: The government has raised the EPF wage ceiling to ₹25,000 per month from ₹15,000, bringing over 5.1 million additional employees under social security. This move also increases employer contribution obligations. The revised ceiling is effective September 17.

articles.headline: Reverse 67% hike in gold hallmark fee: Jewellers
articles.summary: Jewellers have criticized the 67% increase in gold hallmarking charges, urging its immediate review. They argue that volumes have expanded significantly and enforcement against fake hallmarking should be prioritized over raising fees, which disproportionately affect lightweight jewelry.

articles.headline: When patience stops paying: IBC’s long wait drives creditors elsewhere
articles.summary: A decline in IBC case admissions and closures, coupled with lengthy resolution and liquidation processes, is pushing creditors to seek alternatives. The prolonged delays erode enterprise value, suggesting the IBC's effectiveness is hampered by its slow pace, impacting its attractiveness to lenders.

articles.headline: The Modi way is to build coalitions in a fractured world
articles.summary: Prime Minister Modi's diplomatic style involves personal engagement, pragmatic alliances, and a focus on India's interests. He builds coalitions by finding common ground on trade, technology, and energy security, strengthening India's voice on the global stage and fostering relationships across diverse geopolitical camps.

articles.headline: The Story Map: A Proven Storytelling System That Makes Your Audience Listen, Believe and Act
articles.summary: Sandeep Nair's 'The Story Map' provides a framework for effective storytelling, breaking down narrative into Soul, Body, and Spirit. articles.summary: EPFO increased the wage ceiling for mandatory contribution from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month, bringing over 1 crore additional workers into the social security net and likely higher pension payouts.

articles.headline: HC asks govt for review on social media's addictive design
articles.summary: Delhi High Court asked the Centre to clarify if it's considering a policy to regulate addiction-causing design features on social media platforms like infinite scroll and autoplay.

articles.headline: HC slams Assam govt over law 'misuse' in razing 21 homes
articles.summary: Gauhati HC criticized Assam for misusing the Disaster Management Act to justify demolishing 21 homes on private land, terming the action 'illegal and unauthorised'.

articles.headline: Meta admits lapses, govt questions its immunity
articles.summary: Govt told Meta it cannot keep invoking intermediary status and must take greater responsibility after the tech giant admitted lapses in dealing with child sexual abuse material.

articles.headline: FTA with NZ to soon be operationalised
articles.summary: New Zealand parliament voted in favour of the FTA with India, paving the way for its operationalisation next month. It allows duty-free access for all exports from India.

articles.headline: Chicken & booze trail leads cops to rowdy
articles.summary: A month-long hunt for a local rowdy-sheeter, Venkatesh, who posed as a Naxal, ended with his arrest. He was tracked down using his habit of ordering chicken and alcohol.

articles.headline: Newlywed couple on bike dies in hit-and-run crash
articles.summary: A newlywed couple, Darshan (25) and Usharani (21), died in a road accident at Sira in Tumakuru after an unidentified vehicle rammed their motorcycle. Three deaths were reported in separate accidents.

articles.headline: Sweeper plan stuck in trial mode, machines still being tested
articles.summary: Bengaluru's wait for mechanical road sweepers continues as machines remain in trial mode, exacerbating waterlogging issues during heavy rain. Accumulated garbage and silt are clogging drains.

articles.headline: Man, 53, falls for fraudulent bank verification call, loses over 81k
articles.summary: A 53-year-old Bengaluru man lost Rs 81,769 to a bank fraudster posing as a bank representative who sought his details for 'credit card verification'.

articles.headline: BMRCL to decide on 37km-to-11km double-decker plan
articles.summary: BMRCL is considering scaling down the double-decker flyover proposal from 37km to 11km, focusing on shorter stretches at key traffic bottlenecks after RITES advised against the end-to-end structure.

articles.headline: Discarded clothes to get new life at city’s circular textile lab
articles.summary: Bengaluru's first circular textile lab has been set up in Koramangala to transform discarded clothes and textile waste into useful products, promoting sustainability and livelihoods.

articles.headline: Student, 18, electrocuted during idol immersion
articles.summary: An 18-year-old student, Mithun, died of electrocution while removing decorative lighting near a Ganesha pandal at Beerandahalli village in Bangarapet taluk during idol immersion.

articles.headline: 10 Maoists get death for Jhiram Ghati ambush
articles.summary: An NIA court sentenced 10 Maoists to death for the 2013 Jhiram Ghati ambush in Chhattisgarh, where 27 people, including senior Congress leaders, were killed. The court called it a 'planned massacre'.

articles.headline: NLSIU students read Umar Khalid’s letter from prison
articles.summary: Following the postponement of a documentary screening on Umar Khalid at NLSIU, students independently read his letter 'A Day in Tihar Jail' on campus, asserting their right to education and dialogue.

articles.headline: Farmers get 12-mth loan holiday
articles.summary: Drought-hit farmers in Karnataka will receive a 12-month moratorium on agricultural loans, followed by a repayment period of up to five years, under a relief package approved by the SLBC.

articles.headline: Priyank: Can BYV sing full song without teleprompter?
articles.summary: Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge challenged BJP president BY Vijayendra to sing the full Vande Mataram without a teleprompter, escalating the row over the state government's decision to limit the song's singing.

articles.headline: Manipur reels under 12k cr GST loss in 3 yrs of conflict
articles.summary: Manipur's ethnic conflict has caused a loss of over Rs 1,200 crore in GST revenue between 2023 and 2026, sharpening Kuki-Naga tensions and highlighting the fiscal strain on the state.

articles.headline: HC flags long govt cases against disabled soldiers
articles.summary: Supreme Court pulled up the Centre and defence ministry for litigating against disabled soldiers for benefits, citing a 2015 report and a lack of implementation of recommendations.

articles.headline: Daily wage worker awaits wrongful termination case hearing at Raj HC for 22 years
articles.summary: A daily wage worker, sacked in 1999, has waited 22 years for his wrongful termination case hearing at Rajasthan High Court, highlighting severe judicial delays.

articles.headline: US slaps SA with sanctions over ‘bias against whites’
articles.summary: The Trump administration will impose travel bans on South African officials accused of discrimination against whites and other minorities, a move rejected by the SA government.

articles.headline: Sudan gold mine collapse kills at least 67 people
articles.summary: A gold mine collapse in Sudan's Nuhud town has killed at least 67 people. Survivors reported the collapse at the al-Zara gold mine, controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

articles.headline: Nepal adds 1,000 to flood missing list, count tops 6,100
articles.summary: Nepal revised its flood missing list to over 6,100, adding nearly 1,000 names after verification. Rescuers recovered 10 bodies from two hydropower projects.

articles.headline: BLA claims killing 43 Pak military personnel past week
articles.summary: The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claimed responsibility for 13 attacks across Balochistan, claiming to have killed 43 Pakistani military and affiliated personnel over the past week.

articles.headline: US-India cultural bridge closes as Kennedy Center shutters
articles.summary: The Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington DC has shut down due to a legal battle over President Trump's demand to add his name to a memorial, impacting global artistic exchange, including from India.

articles.headline: Satellites show Earth lost over 12 trillion tons of ice
articles.summary: A major scientific report revealed that Earth's ice sheets have lost over 12 trillion tons of ice since 1979, with warmer waters accelerating melting from below and sides.

articles.headline: EU proposes social media ban for kids under 13
articles.summary: European Union proposed banning children under 13 from social media and limiting access for older teens, aiming to protect minors from Big Tech's influence.

articles.headline: Pentagon report reveals hidden cost of US’ Iran war
articles.summary: A Pentagon report estimates the US war against Iran has cost $33.4 billion, including $22.3 billion in expended munitions and $3.7 billion in equipment losses, challenging official narratives.

articles.headline: Saudi: Houthi drone destroyed near Mecca; rebels deny
articles.summary: Saudi air defenses destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered prohibited airspace. Houthis denied targeting Mecca and claimed hits on an oil port and airbase.

articles.headline: Indian couple win damages in UK over separation before deportation
articles.summary: An Indian couple won compensation in London after the high court ruled their separation in detention before deportation was unlawful, violating their right to family life.

articles.headline: Modi to hold Chintan Shivir for 3rd term
articles.summary: PM Modi directed setting up of six groups of ministers for brainstorming ahead of a two-day Chintan Shivir next week, focusing on governance and future agenda.

articles.headline: EC to hear TMC factions today, for 3rd time
articles.summary: The Election Commission has called two TMC factions for a hearing today regarding party ownership and assets, the third such date since the dispute began.

articles.headline: India rejects ‘illegal’ Pak-China border panel
articles.summary: India rejected Pakistan's announcement of a Pak-China Boundary Joint Commission, stating there is no boundary between them and asking Pakistan to vacate occupied areas.

articles.headline: RBI’s FAQs keep Tata Sons boxed
articles.summary: RBI's updated NBFC FAQs effectively keep Tata Sons classified as an upper layer NBFC, rejecting its bid to deregister and effectively preventing it from avoiding mandatory listing.

articles.headline: ‘Art shouldn’t stop artists speaking up’
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran's band withdrew from his US tour in solidarity with rapper Macklemore after he was removed for pro-Palestine remarks. Sheeran stated he respects Macklemore's stance but prioritizes fan experience.

articles.headline: Suriya & Jyotika mark 20th anniversary
articles.summary: Actors Suriya and Jyotika renewed their wedding vows in an intimate Christian ceremony in Scotland to celebrate their 20th anniversary, sharing heartfelt posts on social media.

articles.headline: ‘We should be able to speak about war, about civilians being killed’
articles.summary: Irish band Beoga withdrew from Ed Sheeran's tour in solidarity with Macklemore, who was removed for pro-Palestine remarks, stating they cannot stay silent on 'genocide' and 'occupation'.

articles.headline: I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety & sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy: Ed Sheeran
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran defended his stance on political issues, stating he uses his platform for diplomacy and safety, not political forums, while respecting Macklemore's activism. His band withdrew from the tour.

articles.headline: Rajesh Nataranga returns to stage after 20 years
articles.summary: Kannada actor Rajesh Nataranga is returning to theatre after 20 years with the play 'Maley Nilluvavarege', seeking to renew his energy and challenge himself as a performer.

articles.headline: Bengaluru’s sharing circles make room for difficult conversations
articles.summary: Sharing circles are forming in Bengaluru, offering a safe space for people to discuss difficult topics like family expectations, ageing, and intimacy, focusing on lived experience and empathy.

articles.headline: HC: Non-bailable warrant can’t justify preventive detention
articles.summary: Karnataka High Court quashed a detention order under the Goonda Act, observing that a non-bailable warrant for petty offences cannot justify preventive detention.

articles.headline: PVR INOX fined 75k, Forum South Rs 50k for violations
articles.summary: Bengaluru South City Corporation fined PVR INOX and Forum South Mall Rs 75,000 and Rs 50,839 respectively for waste segregation and STP waste violations.

articles.headline: TS Govt plans for 600cr skydeck
articles.summary: Bengaluru's proposed 250-metre-high skydeck, with an estimated cost of Rs 600 crore, is being envisioned as a hub for tourism, entertainment, and commercial attractions.

articles.headline: ‘I’ve been in the industry long enough to know what I want as an artiste’
articles.summary: Actress Shraddha Srinath discusses her career shift towards meaningful roles, trusting her instincts about film teams, and her preference for exploring new locations over commercial success.

articles.headline: Real Madrid squander two-goal lead but win 3-2
articles.summary: Real Madrid let a two-goal lead slip against Elche but secured a dramatic 3-2 victory thanks to substitute Carlos Espi's stoppage-time winner.

articles.headline: Lionel Messi called up for Argentina friendly
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has been called up to the Argentina national team for a friendly against Benin, marking his potential 'last tango' with the national side.

articles.headline: Indian athletes land in Japan to a forgettable welcome
articles.summary: Indian athletes faced accommodation issues, missing accreditation, and transport delays upon arrival in Japan for the Asian Games, tarnishing the host nation's organizational reputation.

articles.headline: Avinash Sable returns to the spotlight
articles.summary: Defending champion Avinash Sable, recovering from injury, is set to compete in the 3000m steeplechase and 5000m at the Asian Games, carrying high medal expectations.

articles.headline: Harmanpreet will rediscover batting form at Asian Games
articles.summary: Former captain Anjum Chopra backed Harmanpreet Kaur to regain her batting form at the Asian Games, emphasizing her importance as captain and player despite recent scrutiny.

articles.headline: Gukesh on fourth board; Jadeja recalled for ODIs
articles.summary: Chess prodigy Gukesh assigned to fourth board at Olympiad; Jadeja recalled for ODIs vs Windies. Jasprit Bumrah rested from T20Is.
